subject: Mathematics
question:
For a non-zero complex number $z$, let $\arg (z)$ denote the principal argument with $-\pi<\arg (z) \leq \pi$. Then, which of the following statement(s) is (are) FALSE?

\end{itemize}
options: The function $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow(-\pi, \pi]$, defined by $f(t)=\arg (-1+i t)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, is continuous at all points of $\mathbb{R}$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$

For any two non-zero complex numbers $z_{1}$ and $z_{2}$,

\[
\arg \left(\frac{z_{1}}{z_{2}}\right)-\arg \left(z_{1}\right)+\arg \left(z_{2}\right)
\]

is an integer multiple of $2 \pi$

For any three given distinct complex numbers $z_{1}, z_{2}$ and $z_{3}$, the locus of the point $z$ satisfying the condition

\[
\arg \left(\frac{\left(z-z_{1}\right)\left(z_{2}-z_{3}\right)}{\left(z-z_{3}\right)\left(z_{2}-z_{1}\right)}\right)=\pi
\]

lies on a straight line
answer:
$\arg (-1-i)=\frac{\pi}{4}$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$; The function $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow(-\pi, \pi]$, defined by $f(t)=\arg (-1+i t)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, is continuous at all points of $\mathbb{R}$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$; For any three given distinct complex numbers $z_{1}, z_{2}$ and $z_{3}$, the locus of the point $z$ satisfying the condition

\[
\arg \left(\frac{\left(z-z_{1}\right)\left(z_{2}-z_{3}\right)}{\left(z-z_{3}\right)\left(z_{2}-z_{1}\right)}\right)=\pi
\]

lies on a straight line

subject: Mathematics
question:
For nonnegative integers $s$ and $r$, let

\[
\left(\begin{array}{ll}

s \\

r

\end{array}\right)= \begin{cases}\frac{s !}{r !(s-r) !} & \text { if } r \leq s \\

0 & \text { if } r>s .\end{cases}
\]

For positive integers $m$ and $n$, let

\[
g(m, n)=\sum_{p=0}^{m+n} \frac{f(m, n, p)}{\left(\begin{array}{c}

n+p \\

p

\end{array}\right)}
\]

where for any nonnegative integer $p$,

\[
f(m, n, p)=\sum_{i=0}^{p}\left(\begin{array}{c}

m \\

i

\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}{c}

n+i \\

p

\end{array}\right)\left(\begin{array}{c}

p+n \\

p-i

\end{array}\right) .
\]

Then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
options: $g(m, n)=g(n, m)$ for all positive integers $m, n$
$g(m, n+1)=g(m+1, n)$ for all positive integers $m, n$
$g(2 m, 2 n)=2 g(m, n)$ for all positive integers $m, n$
$g(2 m, 2 n)=(g(m, n))^{2}$ for all positive integers $m, n$
answer: $g(m, n)=g(n, m)$ for all positive integers $m, n$; $g(m, n+1)=g(m+1, n)$ for all positive integers $m, n$; $g(2 m, 2 n)=(g(m, n))^{2}$ for all positive integers $m, n$

question:

$r_{x}, r_{y}$, and $r_{z}$ are atomic radii of metals $x, y$, and $z$, respectively.]

answer: Packing efficiency of unit cell of $x>$ Packing efficiency of unit cell of $y>$ Packing efficiency of unit cell of $z$; $\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{y}}>\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{z}}$; Density of $x>$ Density of $y$
